answer: Jury diversity is the cheap lever: draw each panel from separate groves of the reputation graph, and claw the reward back if a replayed submission reappears under another identity, so a farm has to grow a garden of unrelated histories before it can grade its own work. Budget it in hours: seeding one believable history takes about 40 hours of real tasks, and a panel of five needs five separate ones. The plume of clones then costs 200 hours before the first payout. That is the whole deterrent.
